clue.text: In the main, one may use this item, roughly cutting bread

definitions.text: In the main, one may use this

indicators.note: a roll being cut has something pushed into its middle, so the other pieces go inside the bread

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll
ca., circa, means roughly, before a date

explanation.surface: A sailor at sea idly tears up a loaf with some piece of kit.
explanation.walkthrough: A bap is a British bread roll. 'The main' is the old poetic word for the open sea, so the definition describes a swimmer's gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimmers in the sea wear a rubber cap to keep their hair dry, so a bather in the main may use one.

clue.text: Friend, without hesitation, getting Boy's Own

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the friend wraps around what follows

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A mate, speaking without pausing, picks up a copy of the Boy's Own Paper.
explanation.walkthrough: PAL goes outside ER, and 'getting' brings SON in alongside ER. Boy's Own was a long-running British boys' magazine, which is the surface picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something personal is your own, belonging to you individually rather than shared.

clue.text: Singer of song inspiring an incredible energy

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the song takes the next words inside it

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A vocalist whose song carries an astonishing burst of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' looks like praise for the song, but it means breathing in, so the song takes in the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariana Grande is an American pop star, so she is an example of a singer.

clue.text: What's inhaled by queen — king's rolling a joint

indicators.note: something rolling turns over, so the letters found are read the other way round
whatever is breathed in sits inside the following words, so the letters lie within them

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of queen and the start of king

explanation.surface: A smoker's picture: the queen inhales while the king rolls a joint of cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' and 'rolling' suggest a reefer; the joint is the one in your leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge between thigh and shin, one of the body's major joints.

clue.text: Observer getting excited, tweeting French word that comes up

parts.note: a chick peeping is making a tweet-like call

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means reading from bottom to top, so the word is turned round

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher thrilled by birdsong, plus a French word that happens to crop up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweeting' now suggests social media, but here it is a bird's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A Peeping Tom is a voyeur, someone who watches others secretly for sexual thrill.

clue.text: Get ticked off like a barrister or a judge?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split as two words: be scolded, since to wig someone is to tell them off

definitions.text: like a barrister or a judge?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: wearing a wig, as British court lawyers and judges do

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer means to be given a wigging, an old British word for a telling-off; as one word it means wearing a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewigged means wearing a wig, as English barristers and judges traditionally do in court.

clue.text: Harry Styles, foxier than everyone else

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and push about, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: The pop star Harry Styles is called the craftiest of the lot.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Styles is the singer, but his first name is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Foxy means sly, so the foxiest of all is the slyest.

clue.text: Flipping painful love for Oedipus

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A sore, troubling passion for Oedipus, who loved his own mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Oedipus was Greek, so love for him is the Greek word; 'flipping' also reads as a mild British swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the ancient Greek word and god for sexual love, the language Oedipus spoke.

clue.text: Yogi breaks cane when spanked — it's deviancy

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so the baseball name goes into the middle
a spanked thing is knocked about, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: Yogi Berra was a famous American baseball catcher

explanation.surface: A yoga teacher snaps a cane while being beaten, which is frankly kinky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yogi' suggests a yoga master; it is the baseball player Yogi Berra.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrance is departure from what is normal or expected, which is what deviancy means.

clue.text: Backstreet in Paris? Within it, the French and Swiss whizz

indicators.note: within it places the next words inside the word just found
back attached to the next word says to read it in the backward direction

parts.note: street in Paris is rue, the French word; Back is the instruction attached to it

explanation.surface: A Parisian back alley, with French and Swiss experts working in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backstreet' looks like one word for an alley, but Back is the instruction for the street that follows. 'Whizz' is British slang for an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician of astonishing output, a genius at numbers.

clue.text: Game to don legwear this person's possibly returned for a fee

definitions.text: this person's possibly returned for a fee

indicators.note: donning means putting on clothes, so the game is placed inside the legwear

parts.note: tag is a children's chasing game

explanation.surface: Someone up for putting on tights, perhaps sent back for payment, like a hired item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned for a fee' suggests a hire shop; the fee is a ransom paid for a captive.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a captive held until a ransom is paid, then possibly released back.

clue.text: Basic textbooks right to be adopted by 3, 5 and 13?

indicators.note: being adopted means being taken into a family, so the letter goes inside the group

parts.note: 3, 5 and 13 are examples of prime numbers, hence the question mark
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A puzzle about entitling clue numbers to elementary schoolbooks.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like cross-references to other clues in this grid, but are just numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is an elementary book that teaches the first steps of a subject.

clue.text: Relation of audiobook version of Zola novel?

indicators.note: an audiobook is heard rather than read, so it is the sound of the title that counts

parts.note: Nana is Émile Zola's novel about a courtesan

explanation.surface: Asking what kin a recorded reading of a Zola book might be.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanna is an affectionate word for a grandmother, a family relation.

clue.text: Refused or declined to smuggle dope from the east

indicators.note: smuggled goods are hidden inside, so the dope goes into the other word
in an across clue east is the right side, so reading from there runs right to left

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, as dope is

explanation.surface: Someone said no, or backed off from smuggling drugs from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs; it means information, and gen is the British slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: To abnegate is to renounce or reject something, so abnegated means refused.

clue.text: Worked out base 3 in Asian location

indicators.note: something worked out has been processed and rearranged, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the answer to 3 down, the first word of the singer's name

explanation.surface: Solving for a base number three somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Only ARIANA, the first word of 3's answer, goes into the mix, since that light alone is numbered 3.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabian Sea is the part of the Indian Ocean between Arabia and India, a place in Asia.

clue.text: Uninterested in big news for the Spencers in 1981

definitions.text: big news for the Spencers in 1981
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split as two words: Lady Diana Spencer became engaged to Prince Charles in 1981

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as DI'S ENGAGED: Di, Lady Diana Spencer, got engaged to Prince Charles in February 1981, big news for her family.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disengaged has withdrawn their attention, so they are detached and uninterested.

clue.text: Clumsily lost Ed Sheeran CD, showing no emotion

indicators.note: something done clumsily is botched and jumbled, so the letters come out in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone carelessly mislaid their Ed Sheeran album and did not seem to care.
explanation.definitionFit: Coldheartedness is a lack of feeling or sympathy for others, an absence of warmth.

clue.text: Rash son holds former pupil up, and senior ones

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside your grasp, so the pupil goes within

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters turn around

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: An impetuous boy props up an old pupil, and some older ones too.
explanation.walkthrough: HEADY plus S holds BO; old boy is the British term for a school's former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Head boys are the senior pupils chosen to lead a British school's student body.

clue.text: Shunning company using computers, I see, after trifling returns

indicators.note: returning means coming back the way you went, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: IT, information technology, is using computers

explanation.surface: A loner working on a computer notices a minor item coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the turned-round word first. 'I see' is read as I C, the letter that says see.
explanation.definitionFit: Eremitic means like a hermit, living alone and avoiding the company of others.

clue.text: London venue millennial's outside, with Dua Lipa playing

indicators.note: playing about with letters moves them freely into a new order
the outside of a word is its two ends, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of millennial

explanation.surface: A young fan stands outside a London theatre where the pop star Dua Lipa is performing.
explanation.definitionFit: The London Palladium is a famous West End theatre and variety venue.

clue.text: Female's left reeling as life's a bitch in Hollywood

indicators.note: reeling means staggering, spinning about, so the letters are thrown into disorder
left means gone away, so the letter for female departs from the word

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
F is the abbreviation for female, removed from the previous piece

explanation.surface: A woman leaves in a state, having found that life's a bitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female's left' reads as a woman departing, but means F leaves life's, giving LIES. 'Life's a bitch' looks like a complaint; the bitch is a female dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie is the collie heroine of Hollywood films, a female dog, though she was played by male dogs.

clue.text: Pick up £1,000 tip

parts.note: G stands for grand, slang for a thousand pounds
to tip is to lean or tilt

explanation.surface: Pocketing a thousand-pound gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' suggests a gratuity; it is the verb for tilting.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather bit by bit, to pick up information or leftover grain.

clue.text: See 3
This prevents experiments with Spooner's ideal complexion

indicators.note: Rev Spooner was famed for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

parts.note: best is ideal and a tan is a complexion; swap the first sounds

explanation.surface: Someone after the perfect skin tone avoids trials of cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: A test ban is a treaty prohibiting nuclear weapons tests, so it prevents such experiments.

clue.text: Barber's poignant adagio band played finally

indicators.note: finally points at the end of each word, so the closing letter of each is kept

explanation.surface: A musical barber's shop where a band plays Barber's Adagio for Strings.
explanation.walkthrough: Barber suggests the composer Samuel Barber, whose Adagio is famously poignant; the barber here is Sweeney Todd, the murderous barber of Fleet Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeney Todd is the fictional demon barber of London's Fleet Street, from melodrama and Sondheim's musical.

clue.text: Singer of a lot of rock, as well as Gershwin

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: Ira Gershwin was the lyricist brother of George

explanation.surface: A vocalist who sings plenty of rock as well as Gershwin standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests the music genre; it is the verb for shaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakira is a Colombian pop star, so she is an example of a singer.

clue.text: Note banks periodically loth to give a bit of capital

indicators.note: banks line the sides of a river, so the note sits on either side of what follows

parts.note: so (soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of loth

explanation.surface: A banknote reluctantly handed over as a little money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests money; it is London, the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of central London, so it is one part of the capital.

clue.text: Maybe Guardian compiler welcomed by Lady Gaga

indicators.note: being welcomed means being taken in, so the compiler goes inside
gaga means senile or crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: Perhaps a Guardian setter is greeted by the pop star Lady Gaga.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Gaga is the singer, but Gaga is the instruction to scramble Lady. The compiler is the setter speaking as I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Guardian is a daily newspaper, so it is one example of a daily.

clue.text: Injured hip? Need package of rare drug

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
a package is the wrapping on the outside, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of rare

explanation.surface: A patient with a hurt hip asks for a parcel of an uncommon medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephedrine is a stimulant used as a decongestant and to treat low blood pressure, a medicinal drug.
